Et in persona totius Christi, quasi de spelunca ad Deum clamantis, ait: *Deprecatus sum.* [n: (AUG.)] Quod dicit *clamavi, exponit, deprecatus sum.* Quasi dicat: Clamor [1065A] meus deprecatio est, non murmur, non blasphemia.

VERS. 3.-- *In conspectu ejus.* [n: (AUG.)] Dominus redditurus est, in occulto ora; unde in Evangelio: *Tu autem cum oraveris, intra in cubiculum tuum, et clauso ostio ora Patrem tuum qui videt in abscondito,* etc. [n: (Matth. VI.)]

VERS. 4.-- *Et tu cognovisti.* [n: (ID.)] Hoc addit, ne audientes, *defecit spiritus meus,* putarent eum dejectum. Ac si diceret: Si illi putant me dejectum, quia spiritus meus defecit, tu me stantem vides, cujus Spiritus me vivificat.

*Semitas.* Justitiae, quas illi non vident.

*In via.* Multae viae, quia multa praecepta: una via, quia omnia ad unum, id est charitatem, rediguntur.

[1065B]AUG.) *In via,* secundum votum eorum; juxta viam, secundum veritatem. Christus enim est via, qui non sinit eos laqueum ponere *in via,* ut non sit nobis quo eamus; sinit tamen ponere juxta viam, ne a via declinemus.

VERS. 5.-- *Considerabam ad dexteram.* [n: (AUG.)] Quam mali non videbant; et hoc est, *et non erat qui cognosceret.* [n: (CASS.)] Cum enim pateris omnia, quis novit quid attendas? [n: (AUG.)] Qui in dexteram attendit, videt; qui in sinistram, excaecatur. Vel, apostoli non stabant ad dexteram, quia carnali timore dispersi sunt, sed ego perstiti.

*Periit fuga.* Tam corporis quam mentis. *Et non est qui requirat.* [n: (CAS.)] Quia nulla est consolatio, sed solus ad passionem relictus est. *Periit fuga.* [1065C] [n: (AUG.)] Circumclusum se dicit. *Periit fuga,* quia non fugit animo, corpore licet aliquando. Circumclusus non fugit corpore, quia non potest. Fortius non fugit mente, qui non vult. *Periit fuga* concluso vel forti; fuga quidem, unde dicitur in Evangelio: *Videt lupum venientem et fugit [n: (Joan. X)]*. Ubi Dominus mercenarium vituperat. Sed alia est fuga corporis, quam Dominus permittit dicens: *Si vos persecuti fuerint in una civitate, fugite in aliam [n: (Matth. X)]*.

*Et non est qui requirat animam.* Quaeritur anima aut a persecutoribus, aut a dilectoribus. Sic fuga perit duobus modis, et a capto et a forti.

VERS. 6.-- *Clamavi.* [n: (CAS.)] Secunda pars ubi agit de fine malorum. *Spes mea.* Quia te ex omnibus eligo. *Portio.* Humiliter dicit et communiter portionem [1065D] sibi esse in terra viventium, cum tota sit sua. Hoc patet ex hoc quod latroni dixit: *Hodie mecum eris in paradiso:* qui est terra viventium aeternaliter.

VERS. 7.-- *A persequentibus me.* Diabolus enim per vasa sua, id est per filios diffidentiae, agit persecutionem corporis, ut intus fiat cordis ruina.

VERS. 8.-- *Educ de custodia,* etc. [n: (AUG.)] Ex persona Ecclesiae loquens, exponit unde liberandus. Alias *de carcere.* Quia in corruptione (quae est poena corporis) angustiatur: post quas angustias in domo Dei tota vita erit confessio, id est laus Dei; modo impedit carcer confiteri. Hic carcer vel spelunca mundus potest dici, ubi omnia vana: unde rogat [1066A] educi animam, quae inde multa patitur, etc., *usque ad* sed corruptio ejus, et tentatio, carcer est.



## PSALMUS CXLII.

*Psalmus David.* Psalmus iste septimus poenitentialium, qui ideo sunt septem, ut eodem numero quo peccavimus, peccata diluamus. [n: (CAS.)] Sicut enim in hebdomada mundi hujus peccamus, ita hoc numero psalmorum remedium poenitentiae peccatis opponitur. In quibus psalmis talis est forma, quia a lacrymis incipitur, et in gaudio finis est, ne quis de venia desperet. [n: (AUG.)] Sicut Absalom David, sic Judas Christum, falsi fratres corpus ejus; vel illiciti motus et operatio.

VERS. 1.-- *Domine, exaudi,* etc. [n: (CAS.)] Primo [1066B] captat exordium; secundo narrat mala sua, et quid contra egerit, ibi, *quia persecutus est;* tertio ponitur deprecatio causis confirmata, ibi, *velociter exaudi;* quarto ponitur laeta conclusio, ibi, *spiritus tuus.* Monet ad poenitentiam, et orationem, ad orandum. In persona totius Christi dicit: *O Domine,* etc. *In veritate tua.* [n: (CAS.)] Non est hoc contra humilitatem, quae petebat audiri: sed veritas et justitia Dei est, ne cum rogante disceptet, ne eum qui se damnat judicet; unde subditur: *et non intres,* non petivit justitiam judicii. [n: (AUG., CAS.)] *In veritate tua, in tua justitia.* Vel justitiam et veritatem dicit, quae parcit poenitentibus, et se damnantes absolvit, et accipit pro eodem *veritatem et justitiam.* Et est, *in veritate tua, et tua justitia,* id est secundum justitiam et [1066C] veritatem quam poenitentibus et se accusantibus indulges.

VERS. 2.-- *Et non intres in judicium.* [n: (AUG.)] Intrant in judicium cum Domino, qui suam justitiam constituunt, quod non iste humilis; unde propheta: *Quid vultis mecum in judicio contendere? Omnes dereliquistis me, dicit Dominus. Cum servo tuo.* Indignum est cum servo, ne dicam cum amico: et si tu dicis amicum, ego servum, fugitivus redeo, pacem quaero, *non sum dignus vocari filius tuus.*

VERS. 3.-- *Quia persecutis.* [n: (CAS.)] Secunda pars, ubi est narratio malorum quae patitur, et quid contra egerit.

VERS. 6.-- *Memor fui.* [n: (AUG.)] Hoc dicunt membra, etc., *usque ad* sed non esse coepisti. *Meditatus [1066D] sum.* Quia utique omnia bona sunt, in quo percipit, quia quidquid in se boni est, a Deo est. *In factis manuum.* Ac si dicat: Quaesivi in opere artificem, et in conditis omnibus conditorem: creatura tua facta est mihi spectaculum.

*Memor fui dierum.* [n: (CAS.)] Recolens iste quod fecit coelum et terram, et quod benefecit antiquis, obliviscitur miseriarum mundi. Et ex his quae Deus fecit se consolatur.

VERS. 7.-- *Velociter.* [n: (CAS.)] Tertia pars, ubi ponitur deprecatio causis confirmata. *Defecit spiritus.* [n: (AUG.)] Impleat me tuus Spiritus, quia defecit meus: jam sum pauper spiritu. In quo enim vivit spiritus suus, ille superbus est spiritu suo, et extollitur [1067A] contra Deum. Unde alibi: *Auferes spiritus eorum, et deficient [n: (Psal. CIII)]*. *In lacum.* Ille descendit in profundum, quia etiam perdit confessionem, ut qui proponit sibi licentiam peccandi sine spe veniae, habenis iniquitatis effusis. Talis non audit Deum dicentem: *Convertimini ad me, et ego convertar ad vos [n: (Zach. I)]*.

VERS. 8.-- *Mane.* [n: (CAS.)] Post noctem peccatorum. [n: (AUG.)] Mane est, cum peccata laxantur. *Notam fac mihi viam.* Hoc fecit Deus, etc., *usque ad* perveniemus ad lumen purum, ad Verbum in principio apud Deum. *Animam.* (CAS.) Ut vas ad fontem attuli: imple ergo.

VERS. 10.-- *Spiritus tuus bonus.* [n: (CAS.)] Quarta pars, ubi est laeta conclusio. *Propter nomen tuum, [1067B] Domine, vivificabis me in aequitate tua.* Gratia Dei hic commendatur: quia non ex meritis, sed ex nomine, quod est Jesus, se vivificatum dicit, sed cum hoc gratia aequitatis miseretur, quia licet Deus omnia gratis faciat, justitiae tamen ejus est supplices justificare, quos daemones videt impetere.



## PSALMUS CXLIII.

VERS. 1.-- *Psalmus David ad Goliam.* [n: (CAS.)] David, Christus totus, etc., *usque ad* et sic caput ejus gladio suo inciditur.--David Goliam, Christus occidit diabolum, etc., *usque ad* unde spiritualiter sequens psalmus, *laudatio* intitulatur.

*Benedictus.* [n: (CAS.)] Triumphalis psalmus, etc., *usque ad* precans per eum liberari, ibi, *Deus canticum.*

[1067C] *Qui docet manus meas.* [n: (AUG.)] Id est qui per Spiritum sanctum, etc., *usque ad* quod sequitur. *Misericordia mea.* [n: (CAS.)] Quia prolixum est multis causas explicare, breviter singulis verbis tangit, etc., *usque ad* quia cum despectu et sub admiratione subditur, *Domine, quid est homo quia,* etc. [n: (AUG.)] *Misericordia mea.* Quia tu das mihi ut misericors sim, etc., *usque ad* dimitte ergo, et dimitto; da, et do.

VERS. 3.-- *Quia reputas eum?* [n: (AUG.)] Magnum est quod Deus aestimat, et tanti facit, ut pro eo Filium dederit, cui etiam fit panis, qui est panis angelorum: non enim sic aestimat hominem Deus, ut homo, qui charius emit equum quam hominem.

VERS. 4.-- *Vanitati similis factus est: dies ejus [1067D] sicut umbra.* [n: (ID.)] Quando homo conditus est, veriteti simlis factus est, vanitati peccando. Vana sunt omnia transitoria, comparatione semper manentis veritatis. [n: (CAS.)] Vanum est, quod de sua substantia cadens vanescit: ut fumus, ut umbra. Ita et ipse homo tabescit, unde subdit, *Dies ejus,* id est vita ejus notoria, id est transitoria, sic praeterit sicut umbra.

VERS. 5.-- *Domine, inclina.* [n: (AUG.)] Humilis David ex persona Ecclesiae, plenus gratia praesumens de Deo, pugnans hic invocat adjutorium Dei. Quasi, in lucta sumus, sed ne deficiamus. *Domine, inclina.* [n: (CAS.)] *Domine.* Idem aperit, etc., *usque ad* et forma Dei formam servi suscepit.

[1068A]VERS. 7.-- *Emitte manum.* [n: (CAS.)] Ad Patrem verba convertit: *Emitte manum,* id est Christum; *de alto* ubi cum Patre, ut carnem induat. [n: (AUG.)] Vel de secundo adventu agit in persona Ecclesiae. Quasi dicat: Ita fac modo. *Emitte manum tuam de alto,* id est Christum de caelo ad judicium. Veniet enim Dominus in voce angeli, et in tuba Dei descendet de coelo. Deinde ex persona Ecclesiae subdit: *Eripe me,* scilicet, per eam manum. *Et libera,* etc., ut in littera.

VERS. 9.-- *Deus, canticum novum cantabo tibi.* [n: (CAS.)] Secunda pars, ubi quasi ille quem precabatur, victor et liberator venerit, ei se cantare in Novo Testamento et Veteri promittit: et ab eo precatur liberari ab his qui beatitudinem putant in terrenis. [1068B] *Canticum.* [n: (AUG.)] Hoc alio nomine significat legem, quam per quinque lapides significavit.

VERS. 10.-- *Gladio.* [n: (AUG.)] Quas superius dixit aquas, ipsum hic dicit gladium; unde et hic subdit quod ibi: *Et erue me de manu filiorum alienorum. Maligno.* De quo: *Lingua eorum gladius acutus [n: (Psal. LVI)]*. Est et benignus gladius, de quo Dominus ait: *Non veni pacem mittere, sed gladium [n: (Matth. X)]*. Hic est gladius bis actus [n: (Apoc. XIX)], utroque acumine praepotens, scilicet Veteris et Novi Testamenti, quo omnis putredo a membris Christi abscinditur.

VERS. 12.-- *Quorum filii.* Hic, qui sint alieni, et quae illorum dextera iniquitatis, et qualiter locuti sunt vanitatem, exponit. [n: (AUG.)] Felicitatem eorum [1068C] enumerat, haec est dextera eorum, haec est vanitas, quam loquuntur, dum haec dicunt beatitudinem. [n: (CASS.)] *Quorum filii.* Vel, mystice haec possunt intelligi ab illo loco, etc., *usque ad* sed novis erroribus pullulaverunt.

*Filiae.* [n: (CASS.)] Quae non habent vires constantiae.

*Compositae.* Non natura pulchrae, sed ab hominibus compositae. Hae filiae sunt cogitationes vel praedicationes eorum qui non habent veram Ecclesiam, sed similitudinem.

VERS. 13.-- *Promptuaria.* Corda diversis rebus facta: unde pessimas eructationes exhalant, quae fetent.

*Ex hoc in illud.* Instabiles, quia non habent radicem [1068D] veritatis.

VERS. 14.-- *Oves eorum fetosae.* Ad litteram, quia vult eos ostendere caducis rebus haerere. Quasi dicat: Peculium eorum fetosum, cum ipsi fide steriles; unde mystice discipuli eorum, hae oves sunt fetosae, quia ipsi alios plures in errore generant. *In egressibus.* Non in ingressibus, quia totum bonum quod habere videntur, ab eis egreditur cito perituris. *Boves.* Non laboro macri, sed otio pingues, ut his qui affluunt divitiis, eum ipsi sint a veritate jejuni. Vel mystice, boves, magistri terrenis affluunt. *Maceriae.* Quae de solis saxis in hortis sed vel vineis; nec ipsa ruit illis, ideo prosperi.

[n: (CAS.)] *Neque transitus, neque clamor,* turbidus [1069A] interrumpit quietem eorum, etc., *usque ad* quae ducit ad mortem.

VERS. 15.-- *Beatum.* Non inde reprehendit quia his abundant, sed quia pro dextera habent, id est, pro beatitudine: et haec est vanitas quam locuti sunt. His et Abraham, et Isaac, et Jacob, abundavit. Felicitas est sinistra, id est temporalis, mortalis.



## PSALMUS CXLIV.

VERS. 1.-- *Laudatio ipsi David.* [n: (CAS.)] Breviter continet hic psalmus quae in Scripturis divinis late diffunduntur, etc., *usque ad* ne quis in ejus laude errare posset:

[n: (AUG.)] Spiritu sancto implet Deus sanctos, etc., [1069B] *usque ad* ideoque spiritus ejus in servis suis laudet eum, quia laudari se facit.

[n: (CAS.)] Ut septem psalmi poenitentiae, sic et septem spiritus, juxta illud sacramentum quod praecepit Dominus Moysi in tabernaculo septem lucernas ponere, perpetuo lumine lucentes.

*Exaltabo te.* [n: (CAS.)] Primo propheta promittit infinitam laudem; secundo, omnes perfecturos Dei laudem novem modis dicit, ibi, *Generatio et generatio;* tertio, eadem latius explicat, ibi, *miserator.*

*In saeculum saeculi.* [n: (CAS.)] Qui hic non incipit, in futuro mutus erit.

VERS. 2.-- *Per singulos dies,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Qui hic per singulos dies, in aeterno die merebitur laudare continua exsultatione.

[1069C] [n: (AUG.)] Benedicit nunc *per singulos dies,* ut, cum venerit unus sine fines dies, eat ex laude in laudem, sicut ex virtute in virtutem. *In saeculum et in saeculum saeculi.* [n: (CAS.)] De qua laude alibi: *In saecula saeculorum laudabunt [n: (Psal. XXXVIII)]*, quia semper amabunt quem semper videbunt, quia visione nihil delectabilius.

VERS. 3.-- *Nimis.* [n: (CAS.)] Uno verbo dedit cogitare quod non potest capi plene: et ideo nunquam cesses a laudibus.

VERS. 4.-- *Generatio et generatio.* [n: (CAS.)] Secundo, omnes perfecturos laudem Dei novem modis promittit. *Opera tua.* [n: (AUG.)] Si in magnitudine deficimus, vel de operibus laudemus operantem, de conditis conditorem, de creaturis creatorem. [n: (CAS.)] [1069D] Novem sunt opera: potentia, magnificentia, sanctitas, mirabilia, virtus, terribilium magnitudo, memoria, justitia, quae post explicabuntur: ex his quasi locis et seminibus omnis laus trahitur, ad quem modum omnia argumenta de paucitate locorum sumuntur. *Et potentiam tuam.* [n: (AUG.)] Non enim opera laudant, nisi ut virtutem operantis annuntient. Sed quidam eloquentes creaturam laudant, creatoris obliti. Sancti vero laudatores, si opera amant, et laudant magis operatorem: et propter haec illum amant. Si in rebus factis sentitur aliqua species, utilitas, virtus, et laudatur magis in illo qui fecit. Si opera laudas, et te qui es Dei opus. Et occurrit illud: *Non te laudet os tuum, ne arrogans [1070A] videaris [n: (Prov. XXVII)]*. Sed non est arrogantia, quia Deum in te, non te laudas.

VERS. 6.-- *Et virtutem.* Si non minaretur, nulla esset corectio; si vero non blandiretur, nulla esset exhortatio. Est itaque amabilis et terribilis. Dicent ergo virtutem disciplinantis et punientis, si praedicant regnum aeternum, non tacent ignem aeternum.

VERS. 7.-- *Memoriam abundantiae suavitatis tuae eructabunt.* [n: (AUG.)] Ipse per abundantem suavitatem suam prius memor nostri est, nos vocando, gratia sua nos praeveniendo, inde nos ejus.

*Eructabunt* dicit, non manducabunt.

[n: (AUG.)] Manducat qui discit, eructat qui docet: hoc tamen eructat quod manducat. Haec memoria, quia valde dulcis manducanda est et eructanda. Sic ergo [1070B] manduca ut eructes.

VERS. 8.-- *Miserator et misericors.* [n: (CAS.)] Tertio latius explicat quae secundo breviter proposuit. Quasi: Merito in his laudabunt, quia *miserator,* etc. Partes laudis ponuntur hic, quae superius, sed non singulae possunt explicari: quis enim opera vel potentiam ejus plene explicaret? [n: (AUG.)] *Miserator et misericors.* Quibus eam veniam dedit. *Patiens.* His quibus nondum dedit, sed exspectat ut det.

VERS. 9.--[n: (CAS.)] *Miserationes.* Ab operibus incipit, ut miserator dicatur dum cadentes restituit. *Misericors,* natura, etiam dum creat. *Patiens,* hoc sumit de secundo loco laudis, scilicet de potentia, quam laudat, non quod terras suspendit, maria coercuit, stellis coelos depinxit, etc., sed quia tolerat [1070C] peccantes, ut convertantur. *Et miserationes ejus.* [n: (AUG.)] Si enim tollas opera tua mala, et non in te remaneant nisi opera ejus, non te dimittet miseratio ejus: si autem tu non dimittas opera tua, erit ejus severitas in opera tua, cum dicet: *Ite, maledicti, in ignem aeternum [n: (Matth. XXV)]*.

VERS. 10.-- *Confiteantur tibi, Domine, omnia opera tua.* [n: (AUG.)] Laudent sicut ea quae non habent sensum laudandi, qui sunt materia laudis: quia dum inquiris, invenis magnam vim in eis, quae a Deo.

*Et sancti tui.* [n: (CAS.)] Omne quod est confitetur vel per se, vel per rationales creaturas. Vel sancti, id est, angeli et homines. Hoc de sanctitate: ipsa est enim sanctitas Dei, ut ei sancti debeant confiteri.

[1070D]VERS. 11.-- *Gloriam regni.* [n: (ID.)] De mirabilibus ergo sumitur. Quasi: Quam mirabilis enim qui fecit coelum et terram, et diversis bonis implevit.

VERS. 12.-- *Ut notam.* [n: (ID.)] De virtute terribilium hoc sumitur, etc., *usque ad* cui magnifico nil comparatur.

VERS. 13.-- *Regnum tuum,* etc. [n: (ID.)] Laudat de perpetuitate et dominationis effectu. Et sumitur hoc de magnitudine: si magnum est ad tempus imperare, majus est dominationis terminum non habere.

*Fidelis Dominus in omnibus.* [n: (ID.)] De abundanti suavitate hoc sumitur; unde supra: *Memoriam abundantiae suavitatis tuae. Fidelis,* quia adventus dona complevit. Ad abundantiam quoque pertinet [1071A] quod allevat ruentes, erigit elisos; unde recordatio suavitatis habetur, et in laudibus ejus eructatur.

VERS. 14.-- *Qui corruunt.* [n: (CAS.)] A malis suis, quos omnes allevat Deus. Vel, ab his temporalibus, sicut sancti, ut Job, qui in saeculo aliquid perdunt et abjecti fiunt, decidentes sunt: sed hos omnes confirmat, quia septies cadit justus et resurgit; impii autem infirmantur in malis [n: (Prov. XXIV)].

*Et erigit omnes elisos.* [n: (AUG.)] Ad se pertinentes, quia superbis resistit.

VERS. 15.-- *Oculi omnium in te sperant, Domine.* [n: (ID.)] De justitia latius agit, ut qui misericordem audit, justum timeat: et justitiae est ut sperantes satiet corporaliter vel spiritualiter. Non semper enim danda est esca, sed in tempore opportuno: [1071B] multis enim petentibus salubriter differtur. *Et tu das escam illorum in tempore opportuno.* [n: (ID.)] Dat ergo medicus aegro quod convenit, etc., *usque ad* benedicens Deum in omni tempore.

VERS. 16.-- *Aperis tu manum.* [n: (ID.)] Etsi non das aliquando, das tamen opportune: differs quidem, non aufers.

VERS. 17.-- *Justus.* [n: (CAS.)] Ipso nomine justitiam aperit, ut manifeste ostendatur hic laus de justitia esse. *Viae* sunt dispositiones et voluntates, quae omnes justae, etiam si verberat.

*Viis suis, et sanctus in omnibns operibus suis.* Sciendum quod *Viae* ad dispositionem pertinent, opera ad effectum: haec secundum nos dividuntur. Sed apud illum, hoc est velle, quod facere: quia [1071C] ex ejus voluntate res habent esse.

VERS. 18.-- *Prope est omnibus invocantibus eum.* [n: (CAS.)] Propitius, qui ubique, et hoc de justitia.

VERS. 19.-- *Voluntatem timentium se faciet.* (ID.) Concludit de justitia: aequum est enim et diligentes custodire et peccatores perdere.

VERS. 21.-- *Laudationem.* [n: (CAS.)] Expositis omnibus, sequitur brevis conclusio, qua concludit quod non potest explicari.



## PSALMUS CXLV.

VERS. 1.-- *Alleluia.* [n: (CAS.)] Vox ista, quasi musicas salutaris, tanquam harmonia coelestis, quae non solum homines, sed etiam angelos delectat, laudem Dei exprimens. Quae congrue huic psalmo praescribitur, [1071D] ubi vir justus exhortatur animam ad laudem Dei: quia in adversis aliquando, velit nolit, perturbatur anima. Unde supra: *Quare tristis es, anima mea, et quare conturbas me?* Sed ut auferat ei perturbationem, suggerit gaudium de spe, si non in re: *Spera in Deo,* etc. [n: (AUG.)] Haec spe erecta anima Deum laudat hic. [n: (CAS.)] Primo, sibi quasi omnibus consulit laudare, ne in vanis oretur; et quasi acquiescens consilio, asserit se laudaturum ibi ubi poterit plene. Secundo, alios monet non sperare in homine, ibi: *Nolite confidere.* Tertio, docet omnem spem in Omnipotente ponendam, ibi: *Beatus,* etc.

VERS. 2.-- *Lauda, anima mea, Dominum.* Sed [1072A] quaeritur, a quo, cui hoc consulitur? Si dicitur caro consulere animae, non videtur hoc esse verum, cum a meliori et a digniori soleat inferiori dari consilium: caro autem inferior est anima. Anima enim, licet vituperata quia peccatrix, tamen melior dicitur per naturam corpore laudato in suo genere, quia spiritualis natura praestat corpore, quam movet, regit, sensificat, capit: et ipsa infinita, vicina est substantiae Dei. Sic aurum, vituperatum quia sordidum, praeest plumbo in puritate laudatio: sic et malus homo optimo equo. Non datur ergo consilium animae a carne, quamvis domita valde et pacata: quae tamen mortua est propter peccatum. Nec etiam caro mortalis immortali consulit animae, quia semper infra animam est; sed superior pars animae, [1072B] scilicet mens, quae cogitat sapientiam divinam, illi inhaerens et in illam suspirans, videt quasdam sui partes perturbari motibus saeculi, cupiditate terrenorum ad exteriora rapi: unde ad interiora et superiora revocat eam. Se ergo secundum sensualitatem exhortans dicit: *Lauda, anima mea, Dominum.* Quid enim tibi placet in hoc saeculo? Divisa per tot saeculorum rerum amores, collige te ad auctorem: hic tibi pax et securitas. Deinde respondet anima menti, quasi hic praegravata non valens desistere, ut dignum est. *Laudabo in vita.* Hic in morte laudabo tenuiter, quia corpus *aggravat animam, et terrena inhabitatio sensum deprimit multa cogitantem [n: (Sap. IX)]*; hic spes pascit, vita in futuro.

*In vita mea.* [n: (CAS.)] Cum ei perfecte inhaesero, a [1072C] quo separari, ut modo fit, mors est: sed spes consolatur, in qua quodammodo vivens laudat.

*Quandiu.* Non quod aliquando non sit, quia in aeternum erit, et ideo vere diu.

VERS. 3.-- *Nolite confidere,* etc. [n: (CAS.)] Secunda pars. Dato consilio et affirmato, ubi plene laudare poterit, quasi longe remotos, et interim dum mala sunt (quibus turbatur anima), monet non sperare in homine, sed in Deo. [n: (AUG.)] Vel quasi in fine saeculi mente positus: cito finienda docet non amare pro aeternis; quasi et meo exemplo, *nolite confidere,* etc. *In filiis hominum.* [n: (ID.)] In uno filio hominis est salus, et in ipso sperate. Non quia filius hominis est, sed quia Filius Dei est. Non propter illud quod suscepit ex te, sed propter illud quod servavit in se.

[1072D]VERS. 4.-- *Exibit spiritus ejus,* etc. [n: (CAS.)] Prius mundat corda prohibendo a noxiis, ut post salutaria intendat monendo salubria.

VERS. 5.-- *Beatus cujus Deus Jacob.* [n: (CAS.)] Tertia pars, ubi docet totam spem in Omnipotenti ponendam, quem ex factis describit ut gentilitas tam frequenter convicta quiescat. [n: (AUG.)] Remotis noxiis, docet quod salutis est, scilicet in quo sperandum sit. *Adjutor ejus spes ejus.* [n: (CAS.)] Ipsius Jacob sic fuit adjutor, etc., *usque ad* id est, hujus veri Jacob, sicut illius.

VERS. 6.-- *Qui fecit coelum et terram.* [n: (ID.)] Quia et cultoribus daemonum spes est in deo suo, determinat in quo debet esse spes, id est in Christo, et hoc [1073A] usque in finem psalmi ostendit, describendo eum per omnia. *Omnia quae in eis sunt.* Ne quem alium putes creatorem, vel minutissimarum rerum existere creatorem.

VERS. 7.-- *Qui custodit veritatem in saeculum.* [n: (CAS.)] Christus, qui est veritas, omnis homo mendax. *Facit judicium.* Haec duo ad justitiam pertinent. Christus judex vindicat patientes propter nomen suum, et dat escam diligentibus se. *Injuriam patientibus.* [n: (AUG.)] Non omnis molestia est injuria. Quod jure pateris non est injuria, ut quod patitur latro et scelerati alii. Aliud ergo est pati injuriam, aliud supplicium. Supplicium enim jure quis patitur, injuria autem juri contraria est.

VERS. 8.-- *Dominus solvit compeditos.* [n: (CAS.)] Hoc [1073B] ad abundantiam suavitatis.

*Dominus erigit elisos.* Quos diabolus elidit, Dominus erigit.

*Diligit justos.* [n: (CAS.)] Quos locat in aeterna beatitudine.

VERS. 9.-- *Pupillum et viduam suseipiet.* [n: (AUG.)] Omnis Ecclesia gentium adventitia est ad patres, non carne, sed imitando, filia.

*Pupilli* sunt omnes in peregrinatione, quibus est absens pater; et omnis fidelis anima est *vidua* sponso absente: unde et magis patrem et sponsum desiderant, et hos protegit Deus non visus, sed desideratus.

VERS. 10.-- *Regnabit Dominus in saecula.* [n: (CAS.)] Hoc est de magnificentia.

[1073C]Regnabit in nobis, cum corda nostra erunt in eo firma, quod non modo.



## PSALMUS CXLVI.

VERS. 1.-- *Alleluia.* [n: (AUG.)] Hic item ait de laude Dei, ubi propheta monet laudare colligentem Israel.

*Laudate Dominum.* [n: (CAS.)] Primo ostendit quos colligat, et quomodo. Secundo, post praedicta, quasi adhuc haerentes et dubios increpat, ostendens unde possint laudare Deum, scilicet si fuerint humiles, ibi, *Praecinite.--Laudate Dominum.* [n: (AUG.)] Hoc dicitur omnibus gentibus. Et quasi quaereremus qualiter laudabimus, laudis causam attulit, *quoniam bonus est psalmus.* [n: (CAS.)] In laude Dei ipse actus est merces quae in futuro erit; ideo laudandus, quia [1073D] aedificat, sic, quia *disper iones Israel,* id est fidelium, de toto mundo in fine saeculi *congregabit* ad regnum. Et est hic laus de factis mirabilibus. [n: (AUG.)] Haec est tota merces laudantium, etc., *usque ad* modo exerceamur in hac laude bonorum operum.

*Deo nostro sit jucunda,* etc. Non est satis psallere ad hoc ut laus Deo placeat, sed opus est ut per vitae quoque munditiem illi placeamus.

VERS. 2.-- *Aedificans Jerusalem Dominus.* [n: (AUG.)] Vel, accepit *Jerusalem* generalem Ecclesiam, etc., *usque ad* quem Pater misit ad captivitatem nostram redimendam pretio sanguinis.

VERS. 3.-- *Et alligat.* A similitudine medici, etc., *usque ad* et Dominus alligat contritiones. [n: (HIER.)] [1074A] Qualiter Samaritanus ille qui descendebat a Jerusalem in Jericho [n: (Luc. X)], quando vidit vulneratum jacentem in itinere, colligavit vulnera ejus. Caeterum de his qui non obtriverunt cor, dicitur per Isaiam: *Non est malagma imponere, neque oleum, neque alligaturas [n: (Isa. I, secundum LXX)]*. Alligamenta Dei sunt temporalia sacramenta, quibus interim consolationem habemus; quae tunc detrahentur cum erit perfecta sanitas.

VERS. 4.-- *Qui numerat multitudinem stellarum, et omnibus eis nomina vocat.* [n: (CAS.)] Non aliena ut astrologi qui Jovem et Venerem nominant. Vel, typice, de sanctis, quia cuique proprium donum dat; vel, omnes sunt in familiaritate, a similitudine Domini, qui famulorum suorum nomina novit.

[1074B]VERS. 5.-- *Sapientiae ejus,* etc., [n: (AUG.)] Ipsam mensuram, et numerum et pondus, etc., *usque ad* vide quid sequitur, *humilians autem peccat.*

VERS. 6.-- *Humilians autem peccatores.* [n: (AUG.)] Qui enim reprehendunt intelligibilia, ideo sentiunt terrena, de Deo incorporeo corporaliter cogitantes. Haec facit his qui volunt irridere legem antequam noscant. Quia ergo magnum est proficere ad intelligibilia et spiritualia, simus mansueti, pulsemus et faciamus quod sequitur.

VERS. 7.-- *Praecinite.* Sic pervenietur ad intelligentiam, sic imago Deo reformabitur. *Praecinite.* [n: (CAS.)] Secundo, ex praedictis quasi adhuc haerentes increpat et impellit, ostendens unde possint intelligere, si humiles et non superbi. Quasi: Et ut intelligere [1074C] valeatis, *praecinite,* etc.

VERS. 8.-- *Qui operit coelum.* [n: (CAS.)] Memorat opera per quae potestas ostenditur. Ad hoc enim quaedam obscura in Scripturis voluit esse, ut haberent servi Dei quid interpretando influerent super aures et corda hominum, excipientium de nubibus Dei saginem laetitiae spiritualis.

*Servituti hominum.* Praedicatoribus, qui hominibus serviunt. Unde Apostolus ait: *Nos autem servos vestros per Jesum Christum [n: (II Cor. IV)]*. Hi seminant spiritualia et recipiunt ab *excelsis saeculi fenum et herbam,* id est temporalia.

VERS. 9.-- *Et pullis corvorum.* [n: (AUG.)] Omnia enim, quae dantur Ecclesiae a divitibus, fenum sunt.

[1074D] [n: (ID.)] Judaei, qui se solos justos, omnes gentes dicebant peccatores. Et vere patres nostri *corvi,* nos autem non sic remanemus: tamen recte pulli corvorum dicimur et sumus. Corvus non invocat, nos vero dimissi invocamus. [n: (CAS.)] Pulli corvorum dicuntur rore vesci et beneficio aetatis, ignorant paternas escas, id est fetores cadaverum: sic filii paganorum innocentes, qui invocant.

VERS. 10.-- *In tibiis viri.* In composito habitu praesumptuosi et audacis. Per virum enim audacem praesumptorem notat. In tibiis notatur incessus incompositus, *in tibiis viri.* Vel, secundum aliam litteram, *in tabernaculis viri,* id est in conventiculis haereticorum, *beneplacitum erit ei.* Nota quod non [1075A] ait in tabernaculis Dei, sed *viri,* per hoc designans audaciam haereticorum.

VERS. 11.-- *Super timentes,* etc. [n: (AUG.)] Timori spem conjunxit, quia non valet timor sine spe veniae: Judas enim timens, sed desperans, laqueo se suspendit. Qui ergo timet Deum, speret et in eo. Placabis autem si speres in misericordia ejus, atque de caetero ita peccare caveas, ut de praeteritis depreceris ut tibi dimittantur.



## PSALMUS CXLVII.

VERS. 12.-- *Alleluia.* Psalmus iste facit amorem futurae Jerusalem. Aggaei et Zachariae dicitur, qui in captivitate reparationem Jerusalem prophetaverunt, quae, ut Jeremias praedixit, post septuaginta annos [1075B] facta est, id est, post volubilitatem totius temporis, quod septem diebus agitur.

*Lauda, Jerusalem.* [n: (CASS.)] Totus hic psalmus potentiam Dei praedicat. Primo, dicit bona futurae Jerusalem, secundo, dicit quae bona hic dantur sanctis, ibi: *Qui emittit.* [n: (AUG.)] In captivitate adhuc constitutus propheta, etc., *usque ad* qui audivimus sic ructantem.

VERS. 13.-- *Confortavit seras portarum tuarum.* [n: (AUG.)] Nota clausam esse januam admissis prudentibus, et exclusis fatuis virginibus, ut nemo jam exeat vel intret. Et congrue post laudis admonitionem subdit de clausis januis: clausa enim janua Jerusalem secure laudat, quia nemo exiit unde doleat; nemo intrat quem timeat, unde sint scandala.

VERS. 14.-- *Adipe frumenti.* [n: (ID.)] Pane qui de coelo [1075C] descendit: in mundo carne clausus est, sola fide cognitus, tunc videbitur sicut est.

VERS. 15.-- *Qui emittit eloquium suum.* Secunda pars subdit quae munera hic dantur electis, per quae veritas futuri potest agnosci.

*Terrae.* [n: (AUG.)] Ut in terra cognoscatur. Nisi enim mittere verbum terrae, qua gravamur et impedimur a reditu, ad adipem frumenti satiantem non levaremur. In terra enim, ubi laboramus fessi, languidi, pigri, frigidi, scilicet in eremo, non deserit, sed manna *qui emittit eloquium,* etc.

*Velociter currit.* [n: (AUG., CASS.)] Vel usque in velocitatem, id est, a Deo, ut sit ipsa velocitas quo electius vel expressius dici non potuit.

Non ait velox verbum, velox sit velocitate, qua [1075D] plus vel minus participat: sed ipsa velocitate, qua caetera dicuntur velocia, nihil est velocius. Et item quod velox est, ut equus alicui est, non ubique: velocitas vero ipsa ubique est, non est in parte. Ad verbum Dei pertinet non esse in parte, ubique esse per seipsum. Haec est sapientia, *quae attingit a fine usque ad finem fortiter,* non tamen motu locali, sed immobilitate. Sed et de sapientiae spiritu dicitur, *actus mobilis, certus, incoinquinatus;* hoc facit velocitas, ut et ubique semper sit, et nusquam inclausa teneatur. Sed quis ista sufficit cogitare? Est tamen spes ad capiendum verbum, quia praedestinavit nos.

VERS. 16.-- *Qui dat nivem,* etc. [n: (AUG.)] Terrae. Frigescente enim charitate, etc., *usque ad* et hos [1076A] dum vocat ad poenitentiam, *nebulam sicut cinerem spargit.*

[n: (ID.)] *Nebulam sicut cinerem spargit,* etc. Cinis ad poenitentiam pertinet, etc., *usque ad* et qui praedestinavit et ad poenitentiam vocavit. Ad litteram: Spargit Deus nivem quasi lanam, nebulam ut cinerem, crystallum facit ut frusta candidi panis. Est enim crystallum species quaedam in modum vitri, sed candida est: dicitur autem esse nix glacie indurata per multos annos, ut resolvi non possit.

*Crystallum suam,* etc. Id est obstinatos, qui non facile ut nix solvuntur.

VERS. 17.-- *Mittit sicut buccellas,* etc. Alias, *ut frusta panis,* ut pascant alios, ut praedicent veritatem, quam impugnant. Omnes, unus panis; singuli, [1076B] frusta; unde: *Multi unus panis sumus in Christo [n: (I Cor. X)]*. Paulus crystallum fuit, durus et nitidus: durus, quia persecutus Ecclesiam; nitidus, quia in lege peritus. Hanc autem Deus solvit, et factus est panis, qui veritatem docuit. Sed nisi solvat,

*Ante faciem ejus Dei quis sustinebit?* Alias, subsistet. [n: (AUG.)] Frigus est, qui deserit, non vocat, non infundit gratiam: et quis alius solvet? Nullus. Unde Apostolus: *Quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus? [n: (Rom. VII.)]* Quasi dicat: Frigesco, nullus solvit, nisi gratia Dei *emittat verbum suum.*

VERS. 18.-- *Emittet verbum suum, et liquefaciet eam.* [n: (CASS.)] Verbo namque Dei veniente, nec frigus, nec obscuritas, nec duritia desperare potest. Salubriter enim liquefiunt, et fluenta spiritualis beneficii [1076C] profundunt aliis unde bibant, juxta illud: *Omnes sitientes, venite ad aquas [n: (Isa. LV)]*.

VERS. 16.-- *Jacob . . . Israel.* [n: (AUG.)] Vel idem significatur per Israel, etc., *usque ad* quia non fuit missus *nisi ad oves quae perierunt Israel [n: (Matth. XV)]*.

*Judicia sua.* [n: (ID.)] Judicium incipit a domo Dei, etc., *usque ad* tres alios psalmos laudis subjungens, ut in hoc opere gratias Trinitatis eluceat.

## PSALMUS CXLVIII.

VERS. 1.-- *Laudate Dominum de coelis.* [n: (CASS.)] Per paucorum commemorationem universam creaturam hortatur laudare Deum. Sunt quaedam quae [1076D] habent spiritum laudandi Deum in eo affectu quo placet eis Deus: quaedam non habent intellectum, sed quia ipsa bona sunt in ordine suo, et ad pulchritudinem universalitatis referuntur, per se non laudant, sed ab ipsis per attendentes ea laudatur Deus: et ita quodammodo laudant, quia de illis nascitur in nobis laus Dei, ad quam nos hic monet propheta.

VERS. 5.-- *Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt.* [n: (CASS.)] Hoc contra illos qui dicunt mundum Deo coaeternum; sequitur: *Ipse mandavit.* Verbo suo, et creata sunt. Prius dixit, *facta,* postea *creata.* Facere enim et nos possumus, sed non creare. Ipse ergo solus creat, quod est proprium Deitatis. Laus ex operibus

[1077A]VERS. 6.-- *Statuit.* Ex potentia omnipotens est, cujus opera non mutantur.

*In saeculum et in saeculum saeculi.* [n: (CAS.)] Et si coelum novum, Deo tamen bene statuta dicuntur, quae novantur per Christum et meliorata permanent. Et est hic laus a potentia.

VERS. 7.-- *Laudate Dominam.* Secunda pars, ubi, enumeratis coelestibus, descendit ad terrestria. Conversus ergo ad illa, tanquam exhortans nos ut eorum consideratione laudemus Deum, quae considerata aperiunt laudem Dei, ait: O vos qui de terra. *Omnes ubyssi.* [n: (AUG.)] Profunditas aquarum, etc., *usque ad* ipsa ergo, id est, nos consideratione eorum hortatur laudare.

VERS. 8.-- *Quae faciunt verbum ejus.* Hoc ideo [1077B] quia visum fuit quibusdam quod Deus superiora regeret, sed haec inferiora despiceret, sed a casibus regerentur; sed et haec agit Deus, et in his minimis laudatur, et alleluia cantatur.

VERS. 13.-- *Confessio.* [n: (CAS.)] Supra dixit prius de coelo, postea de terra; hic de omnibus simul. Et accipit per coelum omnia superiora, et per terram omnia inferiora. [n: (AUG.)] *Confessio ejus super coelum et terram.* Illum omnia confitentur in se vel in aliis; pulchritudo omnium vox est confitentium in attendentibus ea, id est, attendentes laudent eum, et de terrenis et de coelestibus, quo non est aliquid melius.

VERS. 14.-- *Exaltavit cornu populi sui.* [n: (ID.)] Ecce quod prophetavit Aggaeus et Zacharias. Modo humile [1077C] est in tribulationibus cornu populi sui, sed cum venerit Dominus, exaltabitur.



## PSALMUS CXLIX.

VERS. 1.-- *Alleluia.* [n: (CAS.)] Post omnes creaturas quas in praecedenti psalmo monuit laudare Deum, eo quod ab ipso creatae sunt, hic proprius et specialius Israel invitat ad novum canticum pro novitate sibi facta, quae mirabilior est Dei operatio: haec est sanctificatio Israel, per quam de veteri factus est novus.

*Cantate Domino,* etc. [n: (CAS.)] Primo multis modis monet laudare regem qui eis benevolus et benficus. Secunda agit de gaudiis sanctorum, ibi, *Exsultabunt.* [n: (AUG.)] Qui vult cantare hoc canticum, diligat aeterna, [1077D] ut fiat novus. Vetus enim homo vetus canticum cantat de terrenis. Novus homo novum cantat de spiritualibus; canticum scilicet pacis, eanticcum charitatis et jucunditatis. Quisquis enim sequitur veterem animositatem, non novam charitatem, novum canticum non cantat.

*Laus ejus in Ecclesia.* [n: (CAS.)] Hic ubi et a quibus cantari debat hoc canticum determinat.

VERS. 2.-- *In rege suo.* [n: (ID.)] Id est, in Christo, qui est rex et sacerdos. [n: (AUG.)] Ut rex pugnavit pro nobis de cruce, diabolum vincens: ut sacerdos, se pro nobis obtulit, nihil inveniens in hominibus quod pro eis offerret.

VERS. 3.-- *In choro.* [n: (ID.)] Quia nulla dispersio, [1078A] sed charissima unitas; tunc exsultatio erit de tympano et psalterio, non ipsius actus.

VERS. 4.-- *Quia beneplacitum est Domino.* [n: (ID.)] In prima conditione rerum legimus omnia placuisse Deo, etc., *usque ad* vel cum parem angelis faciet.

VERS. 5.-- *Exsultabunt sancti.* [n: (ID.)] Secunda pars, ubi agit de gaudiis sanctorum et potestate. *Gloria.* Est bonorum actuum frequens laudatio, de quibus justi laetantur in cubilibus, id est in conscientia, ideo quia habent tam bonum Dominum, qui dat peccantibus gratiam et in meritis vitam aeternam. Fatuus extra in fabulis hominum laetatur; sanctis hic modus gaudii est, ut ad illum referantur bona qui dedit.

VERS. 6.-- *Exaltationes.* [n: (ID.)] Virtus Dei et potentia praedicatur in gloria sanctorum. In cubilibus, [1078B] in diversis mansionibus est gloria sanctorum. De quibus Dominus. *In domo Patris mei mahsiones multae sunt. [n: (Joan. XIV.)]*

*In gutture.* Qui in corde et in lingua non desinunt laudare eum, a quo aeterna habent.

*Gladii.* Potestatem verbi Dei accipientes, cum Domino judicabunt, sedentes super duodecim sedes; et tunc vere fiet *vindicta et increpatio in populis,* tunc reges terrae ligabuntur: unde nos sit liberum exire. Et nobiles ferent ferrea vincula, ut gravia ad portandum, et quae non possunt rumpi: et sic fiet judicium conscriptum, id est ab angelis comprobatum. De quo Apostolus: *Neseitis quia angelos judicabimus? [n: (I Cor. VI.)]* Et ne putes solos apostolos judicare, addit, *gloria haec,* scilicet potestas judicii, est omnibus [1078C] sanctis ejus, id est perfectis, qui pro Christo omnia terrena reliquerunt.

[n: (AUG.)] *Exaltationes Dei in gutture.* Sic enim laetantur in cubilibus et faucibus, id est in corde et lingua, ut non sibi tribuant quod boni sunt, sed Deo, a quo acceperunt quod sunt, et sperant id quod nondum sunt.

VERS. 8.-- *Ad alligandos.* His vinculis mandatorum et praeceptorum Dei ligantur gentium reges, nobiles saeculi, ab infirmis et contemptibilibus hujus mundi, quos elegit Dominus ut fortia quaeque confunderet; ipsosque implevit Spiritu sancto, et dedit eis frameas bis acutas, ut ad Christi timorem nobilium corda converterent, et saeculari nobilitate [1078D] contempta, paupertatem eligerent et nobilitatem in Christo. Voluit enim prodesse imperatori de piscatore, non piscatori de imperatore.

[n: (AUG.)] Per hos ligat reges et nobiles in vinculis ferrcis, ne progrederentur ad illicita.

## PSALMUS CL.

VERS. 1.-- *Laudate Dominum.* [n: (CAS.)] De laude Dei in sanctis ejus, qui glorificati sine fine laudant. Monetur civitas Dei, scilicet unitas omnium sanctorum, ore et animo cantare. In hoc culmen omnis psalmodia perducitur, quae nuptiali dulcedine cantatur.

*Laudate eum in firmamento.* [n: (AUG.)] Virtus est in [1079A] firmamento, etc., *usque ad* qui invicem se honorantes, dant laudem Deo.

[n: (CAS.)] Quibus propheta in principio formam conversationis ostendit, jam in illa Jerusalem receptis, dicit in eis laudandum esse Deum, qui omnia dedit. *In firmamento,* quia morte sua diabolum vicit, et credentes ad coelum perduxit. In virtutibus vel potentatibus, quia omnia subjecta pedibus ejus.

VERS. 2.-- *Secundum multitudinem magnitudinis ejus.* Quomodo hoc, cum magnitudinis ejus non est finis? sed spiritualibus et sanctis dicitur hoc. Et cum non sit finis magnitudinis, secundum eam laudatur. Deus, cum sine fine laudetur. Quomodo autem debeat laudari, per similitudines mysticas usque ad finem psalmi dicit: *Tuba* concrepet regi, *psalterium* canat [1079B] Deo: *cithara* cum reliquis sponso. Tuba enim terribilis, vel in bello sumitur, vel, in adventibus regum apparatur; psalterium a summo, cithara ab imo sonat: haec omnia, humanis actibus comparata, figuraliter ibi dicuntur laudes Dei personare.

VERS. 4.-- *In chordis et organo.* [n: (CAS.)] *Chordas* ponit pro omni instrumento musico, quod chordarum tensione sonat. *Organum* est quasi turris fistulis diversis fabricata, flatu follium sonans; et ut haec [1080A] omnia de hominibus acciperes, ad hominis os venit: et exponens quid sit laudare *in chordis et organo* subdit.

*Laudate eum in cymbalis,* etc. *Cymbala* bene sonantia labia nostra sunt quae cordi concinna in laudibus Dei bene sonant, in quibus est similitudo cymbalorum, et harmoniam reddunt, et ideo bene inter musica instrumenta sunt. [n: (CAS.)] Cymbala bene tinnientia sunt ex permistis metallis parvissimae phialae, quae acutum sonum reddunt. Sed quia omnia spiritualiter intelligi vult, apto fine concludit:

VERS. 6.-- *Omnis spiritus,* angelicus et humanus, *laudet Dominum.* Non caro et sanguis, non habitus saeculi: sed quod est in natura rerum sublimius, [1080B] quod coelestia sapit, aeterna capit. Brevis et perfecta scientia, ut Deum spiritualiter omnia laudent, in his totius musicae perfectio est. Est enim flatus in tuba, pulsus in cithara et in cymbalis, vox in choro. Quibus musicis instrumentis significatur spiritualis harmonia, quae non auribus, sed pura mente advertitur.

[n: (AUG.)] Tria sunt genera, etc., *usque ad* vitae aeternae vox est: *Omnis spiritus laudet Dominum.*
english:
## THE PROLOGUE OF BLESSED JEROME ON THE BOOK OF PSALMS.

[n: ( Vide Operum ejus tom. VIII. )]



## PROTHEMATA ON THE PSALTER.

[0841A] [n: (AUG.)] This book is entitled among the Hebrews the Book of Hymns, for this reason, that a hymn is where words and praise are held together with a song, which is found in the psalms. It is also entitled, according to some, the Book of Soliloquies: which seems to be so done for this reason, that what a man searches out with himself, and learns from none save from the truth presiding within him, is called a soliloquy, for example, in the manner in which blessed Augustine searched out with himself concerning the nature of the soul and concerning the nature of God, in the same way the Prophet may be said to have searched out with himself concerning the incarnation of the Son of God, and concerning the repairing of the human race. King David and prophet, when he was reigning prosperously, wishing to magnify the worship of God, when at last he was bringing back to Jerusalem the ark that had been given back by the Philistines and had for a long time [0841B] afterward wandered in uncertain seats, went before it naked with the harp [n: (II Reg. VI)]: but he had also chosen four thousand men who should sing psalms not only with the voice but also with musical instruments: over whom he set four, Asaph, Idithun, Eman, Ethan, or the sons of Core, who, falling away from the crime or sacrilege of their father, whom the fire had consumed [n: (Num. XVI)], stood on most devoted in the worship of God.

[n: (HIERON.)] The psaltery is a certain musical instrument put together in the shape of the letter Δ: and from that musical instrument (by which the present work was set to measure) it took its name to itself. The psaltery is called among the Hebrews *nebel* (נבל), among the Greeks ψαλτήριον, but among the Latins *organum.* Many say that David [0841C] did not make all the psalms, because certain of them are entitled in the person of others. But, as blessed Jerome says, they are not to be listened to in this. For David composed all the psalms: he moreover appended them, wherein he had many helpers, over whom he set four, namely Eman, Ethan, Asaph and Idithun. By divine counsel this was done, that the psalms should be entitled in the persons of others, either for the interpretation of the names only, or for the business in hand, or for both. For the interpretation of the names only, as in the person of Idithun; for the business, as in the person of Aggeus and Zacharias; for both, as in the person of Solomon; Idithun, Asaph, the sons of Core and the rest of this kind were not authors of the psalms, but were set over the craftsmen who sounded the psalms [0841D] in three ways: either by the human voice, or by musical instruments, or commonly in both ways. And this in two manners, either by the instrument after the voice, or by the voice after the instrument: whence their names, that they might take [0842A] honour from the ministry, are inserted in the titles, chiefly for the signifying of things. But a psalm is the sound of the instrument, a canticle the singing of the human voice in the praise of God; a canticle of a psalm, when the voice comes after the instrument, a psalm of a canticle, when the instrument comes after the voice.

[n: (CASS.)] It is commonly asked: why are the psalms read in the Church before other Scriptures? This is for the reason that of old among the Hebrews this custom obtained in the temple of God. Or, because the psalms contain more of mysteries than the other Scriptures, and say many things briefly, in which the whole law and the prophets and the Gospel consist.

[n: (CASS.)] Prophecy is a divine inspiration or revelation, which declares the outcomes of things, whether by deeds or by words, with unmoving [0842B] truth, whence prophecy is *a vision,* the prophet *one that sees.* Now this grace has been given in many ways: either through the works of men, as were the ark of Noe and the sacrifice of Abraham, and the passage of the Red Sea; or through births, as of Esau and Jacob, who signified things to come; or through speaking angels, as they spoke to Abraham, to Lot and to others; or through visions, as to Isaias and Ezechiel, and the rest; or through dreams, as to Solomon, Joseph and Daniel; or through the cloud and the voice from heaven, as to Moses; or in yet other ways. David, however, by none of these, but taught inwardly by a heavenly breathing, with the Spirit speaking in him, was filled full, as in I Kings: « The Spirit of the Lord was directed into David [n: (I Reg. XVI)]. » And the Lord: « If David in spirit calls him Lord, how is he [0842C] his son? » [n: (Matth. XXII.)] But the Holy Spirit was so given to the prophets that at times he withdrew for their sins and returned appeased; and as Peter says: « Prophecy was not at any time brought by human will, but, inspired by the Holy Spirit, holy men of God spoke [n: (II Pet. I)]. » Nor are those strangers to the gift of prophecy to whom is given the faculty of understanding or of interpreting the Scriptures.

[n: (HIERON.)] There are many kinds of anointed ones: the patriarchs were called anointed, as: « Touch ye not my anointed [n: (Psal. CIV)]; » in the Parables, all who came out of Egypt are called anointed. The chrism is made in Exodus, whence the priests are anointed; there is another ointment, with which kings are anointed; but this in two manners, for if it is David and Solomon, that is, *strong of hand* and [0842D] *peaceable,* one is anointed with the horn; if Jehu and Azahel, with the cruse, which is an earthen vessel. But Cyrus also, king of the Persians and Medes, who released Israel, is an anointed one, according to that word: « Thus saith the Lord to my anointed [0843A] Cyrus [n: (Isa. XLV)], » which the words that follow do not permit to be taken of the Saviour, as some suppose. There is a prophetic ointment, with which Elias is commanded to anoint Eliseus for a prophet [n: (III Reg. XIX)]; above all is the spiritual ointment, which is called the oil of gladness, wherewith Christ was anointed above his fellows, who have the chrism of baptism. And if any man lose it, let him not despair; because concerning the separating chrism it is written in Leviticus [n: (Lev. XIII)], that when any man's leprosy has been cleansed, the priest shall put oil for him in his left hand, and the rest of the things that are said there, and let him himself be called the anointed of God. But this remains, that the same man is often anointed, lest there be occasion of ruin to the negligent. For it is enough for the leper that, after the first ointment has been lost, he be anointed a second time; but he is often anointed who is always [0843B] going forward: and, from the oil of the leper, he comes to the ointment of the people; thence to the priestly; from that to the chrism of the bishop; from the bishop to the king; from the king to the patriarchs; from the patriarchs to Christ.

[n: (CASS.)] As prophecy comes about in diverse ways, so also at diverse times. There is therefore one concerning the present, as Elizabeth: « Whence is this to me, that the mother of the Lord should come? etc. » [n: (Luc. I.)] Concerning the past, as Moses: « In the beginning God created heaven and earth [n: (Gen. I)]. » Concerning the future, as: « Behold a Virgin shall conceive, etc. [n: (Isa. VII)]. »

Again, one prophecy is according to the foreknowledge of God, which must in all ways be fulfilled, as: « Behold a Virgin shall conceive, etc. » Another is according to threatening, as: « Forty days, and Ninive shall be overthrown [n: (Jonae III)]. »

[0843C]It is therefore to be noted that the prophet sometimes speaks indiscriminately of things to come as of things present; sometimes of things past, sometimes also properly of things to come: which is done for this reason, that he says all things at the dictation of the Holy Spirit, to whom all things are known, whether past or future, as though present.

[n: (REMIG.)] This book consists of a hundred and fifty psalms, not without the reason of a deeper mystery. For this number is most renowned for mysteries. For it is made up of eighty and seventy, whose beginning and signification come from eight and seven. For the eightfold signifies the eighth, the resurrection: because, whereas there are six ages of the living, the seventh of the dying, the eighth will be of those that rise again. But by the sevenfold is signified the time of this life, which is carried on by the repetition of seven [0843D] days. Rightly therefore has this book been composed of such a number of psalms, because it thus teaches us so to work and to live in the sevenfold of this life that in the eighth of the resurrection we may obtain the robe of glory. Or else because by the eightfold the New Testament is signified: for the fathers of the New Testament serve the ogdoad, observing the eighth day of Christ's resurrection, that is, the Lord's day, the octaves of the saints, awaiting the eighth of the resurrection of the dead. But by the sevenfold the Old Testament, because the fathers of the Old Testament served the hebdomad, that is, the sevenfold, observing the seventh day, the seventh week, the seventh year and the fiftieth, which is woven of seven weeks of years, that is [0844A] the jubilee: whence Solomon: « Give portions to seven, and also to eight [n: (Eccl. XI)]. » Well therefore has this book been published with this number of psalms, whose parts contain the doctrine and the commandments of both Testaments.

[n: (AUG.)] Again, by three fifties a threefold division of the psalms is made, for the signifying of the three states of the Christian religion: the first of penitence, in which also the first fifty of the psalms is ended, namely: « Have mercy on me, O God; » the second of righteousness, in which also the second fifty: « Mercy and judgment I will sing to thee; » the third the state of eternal life, in whose praise the third fifty is finished, namely: « Let every spirit praise the Lord. »

[n: (ID.)] The Book of Psalms is one, not five, as is read in the Acts of the Apostles: « As it is written [0844B] in the book of Psalms » [n: (Act. I)]. Jerome nevertheless says five books, that is, five divisions which are made by « so be it, so be it. »

The order of the psalms disagrees with the order of the history, because David sinned with the wife of Urias, and sang of penitence: « Have mercy on me, O God, » before his son persecuted him and he sang: « Lord, why are they multiplied; » but they are believed to have been so ordered by Esdras the prophet at a divine prompting.

The matter is the whole Christ, bridegroom and bride. The intention, to conform to Christ the new man those men who were deformed in Adam. The manner of treating: sometimes he deals with Christ according to that which is the head, sometimes according to the body, sometimes according to both. According to that which is the head, in three ways: for either according [0844C] to the divinity, as: « With thee is the beginning, etc.; » sometimes according to the humanity, as: « I have slept, etc., » sometimes by transumption, as when he uses the voice of the members, as there: « Far from my salvation, etc. » Again, of the Church in three ways: sometimes according to the perfect, sometimes according to the imperfect, sometimes according to the evil: who are in the Church in body, not in mind; in number, not in merit; in name, not in the divine power.



## PSALM ONE.

VERS. 1.-- « Blessed is the man who hath not gone away, etc. » [n: (AUG., Enarr. in Psal., tom. III.)] The order, Adam went away when he withdrew from God; he stood, when he was delighted with sin; he sat, when, confirmed in pride, he could not return, save as set free by this man, who had none of these things. [0844D] Adam went away when he consented to the persuasion of the devil; he stood, while he ate the apple; he sat, while he excused himself: « The woman whom thou gavest me seduced me. » [n: (Gen. III)] [var: Vulg. Gn 3:12 *Mulier, quam dedisti mihi sociam, dedit mihi de ligno, et comedi*, "The woman, whom thou gavest me as a companion, gave me of the tree, and I did eat"; the printed *me seduxit* imports the seducing that the Vulgate assigns to the serpent at Gn 3:13.]. After the likeness of exiles, who, while they are on the road, are more easily called back, while they now stand, with more difficulty: at length with the greatest difficulty, when they have there been made masters and lords. [n: (REMI.)] There is sinning by thought, by act, and by words in teaching. [n: (CASS.)] The impious man is so against God, the sinner against himself, the pestilent man against his neighbour. « In the chair, giving an example of sinning. » [n: (CASS.)] The throne is of kings, the tribunal of judges, the chair properly of teachers. [n: (Ibid.)] It is as though he said: You who have fallen through the first Adam, be ye conformed to this second one: because the blessed man is the contrary of the first

[0845A]VERS. 2.-- « But in the law. » AUG. [n: (CASS.)] Here he is shown full of every good in himself. [n: (AUG.)] It is not perfect praise to flee the things to be blamed, unless the things to be praised follow. In the order in which they grew in the first man, they are taken away in the second.

« In the law. » [n: (Ibid.)] He who is in the law acts according to the law, he who is under the law is acted upon according to the law: the one is free, the other a slave. [n: (Ibid. AMBR.)] One thing is the law which is written for him that serves, another that which is beheld with the mind by him who has no need of letters. « The will. » [n: (CASS.)] That there be no weariness of labour, nor idleness, but he shall meditate always. The will of sense is under the law; of reason, in the law; of divinity, above the law.

VERS. 3.-- « And he shall be. » [n: (Ibid.)] Here he is shown useful to us, giving the fruit of life, and leaves, and overshadowing us, [0845B] « Blessed is the man. But in the law. And he shall be. » The full definition of the blessed man. All these things belong not to every blessed man, but to Christ alone. « As a tree. » [n: (Ibid.)] After the likeness of the tree of life which is in paradise, whereof obedient man was to have eaten. « A tree. » [n: (Ibid.)] In paradise there is the tree of life, a tree unto life, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. « Of waters. » [n: (AUG.)] The waters are the Holy Spirit, according to that word: « He that shall have believed in me, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water [n: (Joan. VII)], » and it is against the heats of the vices. [n: (CASS.)] Or, by water, the wisdom of God, by which the inner man is restored, as thirst by water. [n: (AUG.)] Or the mortal race, as Job: « Many waters, many peoples, » because they flow down into death, as waters into the sea. « He shall give. » [n: (Ibid.)] To give pertains to the rational sense and to the will of the one offering. [0845C] « And the leaf. » [n: (Ibid.)] As the leaves cover the fruit, so the words of the Lord guard his promises. « And all things. » [n: (Ibid.)] Why go through them one by one.

VERS. 4.-- « Not so the impious. » Here by the vengeance upon the wicked he terrifies the adverse, the dread of these makes what has gone before more welcome. « From the face of the earth. » [n: (AUG.)] Of eternal stability, because as this earth nourishes and holds up a man, so that other earth holds up the inner man.

VERS. 5.-- « Therefore they shall not rise again. » Because the wind casteth them away, that is, therefore, because they have been given over to a reprobate sense: therefore they do not rise again in the first resurrection, that they may judge themselves in counsel, that they may set the wills of God before their own. Or in the council, that is, in the harmonious multitude of the just, the impious idolaters, or apostates. Sinners, false Christians: or else therefore they do not rise again in the time to come, [0845D] that they may judge, or that, being judged, they may rest in the council, that is, in the college of the just. « In judgment, etc. » In the judgment there will be four orders: some shall judge and shall not be judged, as the most perfect; some shall neither judge nor be judged, as the damned unbelievers; some shall be judged and shall be saved, as the moderately good; some shall be judged and shall perish, as the evil faithful. « In the council. » [n: (AUG.)] In the eternal good, to follow which was counsel to the saints. « Or in the council, » in the judgment, that they may judge together with them; for there is judgment when different sins are punished with different penalties; and it is said from this by likeness. « They rise again. » What resurrections these are: of the soul, from sins in the present; of the body, from death in the time to come, whereby it shall be made impassible and immortal.

[0846A]VERS. 6.-- « For the Lord knoweth, etc., » That is, these do not rise again in the soul, because God does not approve their works, but those of the just only.



## PSALM II.

« A psalm. » The modulation that is made by the touching of ten strings is the good work that is done by the keeping of the ten commandments. « David. » [n: (CASS.)] Strong of hand, or fair of aspect, is Christ, who warred down the powers of the air, upon whom the angels also desire to look.

VERS. 1.-- « Why have the nations raged, etc. » [n: (CASS.)] This psalm is the second in order, the first in title; whence in the Acts of the Apostles it is called the first. First he rebukes the persecutors and threatens them, [0846B] and foretells as a prophet. « Vain things. » [n: (Ibid.)] To hold him in death; or, that the world should not go away after him.

VERS. 2.-- « Kings. » [n: (Ibid.)] The former, who slew the infants, is Herod, the latter, he who consented with Pilate in the death of Christ. Kings and princes. [n: (Ibid.)] He could also, according to Ambrose, speak in the plural of one man. For only king Herod and prince Pilate are shown by the voice of Peter, in the Acts of the Apostles, to have conspired against Christ.

VERS. 3.-- « Let us break asunder. » [n: (AMB.)] Or they came together, saying: Let us break asunder their reasonings, that is, of the Lord and of his Christ, or of Christ and of the disciples, by which they wish to bind us to themselves. [n: (AUG.)] And although it might be said otherwise, it fits more openly those who are unwilling that the yoke of Christ be laid upon them. « Bonds. » The promises of eternal life, [0846C] and the threatenings of hell, by which they wish to subjugate us to themselves. « Let us cast away. » Their reasonings being destroyed, let us shake off his dominion from us. [n: (Ibid.)] The yoke, that is, the law: but « he that dwelleth in the heavens. »

VERS. 4.-- « He shall laugh them to scorn. » [n: (Ibid.)] As when he rose again with the guards set: « He shall deride, » when they were scattered through the world. The derision of God is the force of the foreknowledge which God gives to his saints, that, seeing the name of Christ to be in all nations hereafter, they may understand that those men meditated vain things.

VERS. 5.-- « He shall speak to them. » [n: (Ibid.)] He opens it more plainly when he says, he shall trouble them. The anger of God is a motion that arises in a soul which knows the law of God, when it sees that law passed over by an evil man, through which motion many things are avenged: or, the anger of God is the darkening of the mind of the transgressors [0846D] of the law.

VERS. 6.-- « But I. » [n: (CASS.)] Secondly, he brings in his words concerning his almighty kingdom and his unspeakable generation, where we learn of his divinity and his humanity. « King. » [n: (ID.)] So also are the kings of the earth appointed by him. « Preaching upon Sion, » so also are the prophets, « The Son, » so also is Israel, « I have begotten thee. » This to Christ alone.

VERS. 7.-- « The Lord hath said. » The person of him that reigns. « My Son. » [n: (AUG.)] Therefore do I give thee the nations for an inheritance rather than to any obedient servant: because thou art Son by nature, and consubstantial by an ineffable begetting. « This day. » [n: (Ibid.)] Although it might be taken of the day on which he was born according to man, yet, since "this day" signifies [0847A] a presence, let it be taken of the everlasting generation of the wisdom of God.

VERS. 8.-- « Ask. » [n: (AUG.)] It pertains to the taking up of man: which was done for the salvation of men, and according to which he intercedes for us. « An inheritance. » [n: (CASS.)] Inheritance is from lord (herus), because in it he holds dominion with free power.

VERS. 9.-- « Thou shalt rule them. » [n: (AUG.)] Partly thou shalt rule, partly thou shalt break, according to that word: « Behold, this one here is set for the ruin and for the resurrection of many [n: (Luc. II)], » so that he who is just may be justified still: and he who is in filth shall be defiled still [n: (Apoc. XXII)]. » « A rod of iron. » [n: (CASS.)] The power of Christ is the rod of iron; the sinner is the potter's vessel, which is both of clay and easily broken.

VERS. 10.-- « And now, ye kings, understand. » Now, [0847B] that is, by the things that have been said. [n: (CAS.)] Thirdly, on account of these things laid open, he admonishes all to obey humbly, and persuades them from the useful, that they perish not, and from the honourable, because blessed are they that trust in him. In this, after Christ, he speaks as it were an Apostle.

[n: (AUG.)] Or, now that I am appointed king, be not sorrowful, ye kings of the earth; for it is expedient for you to be under him, from whom come understanding and learning, that you may not rule rashly, but may serve the Lord of all, and may exult in blessedness.

VERS. 12.-- « Lest at any time he be angry. » [n: (Ibid.)] The doubt is not according to the prophet, but according to those men themselves, who think upon the anger of God with doubting. « From the just way, » that is, being taken away from Christ, or from good working.

[0847C]VERS. 13.-- « When his wrath shall be kindled. » [n: (CASS.)] Now he does not burn when he chastises, as a father, but in the time to come he will burn, because there will be nothing of patience in the time to come. « In a short time his anger. » Because he examines not each of these things separately, but all of them together.

## PSALM III.

VERS. 1.-- « A psalm, » [n: (AUG.)] concerning the passion and resurrection of Christ: the son is Judas, from whom he fled, when, at his departing, he withdrew with the rest into the mountain; or rather when the wisdom of God forsook his mind, so that he was wholly the devil's, which forsaking is called a flight because of its swiftness. Whence: « That which thou dost, do quickly [n: (Joan. XIII)]. » To him Christ showed peace, as David also did to his wicked son, whence he is called the peace of the father: but Judas, like Absalom, perished by hanging. He sets forth two opposed [0847D] parts. The voice of Christ, as it were wondering, when he came to save: « Lord, why, etc. »

VERS. 2.-- « Lord, why. » [n: (CASS.)] The first psalm of those which treat briefly of the passion and the resurrection, against those men, and chiefly the pagans, who do not think that the glory of majesty can descend to lowly things.

VERS. 3.-- « Many say, etc. » [n: (AUG.)] Or this each man says who is assailed by vices and desires.

« They say to my soul: There is no salvation, etc. » By the heaping up of vices there creeps in a despair of health, as though the vices were insulting the soul; or also by devils and his angels, through suggestions.

[0848A]VERS. 4.-- « Thou art my upholder. » [n: (CASS.)] In Christ. The head, that is, Christ, or the mind which serves the law of God. « Thou hast struck all. » It is rightly said in the predestination concerning the devil and his angels. « Upon the people. » This is each one of us. [n: (ID.)] Or the Church and its head speaks this, set amid the storms of persecutions throughout the whole world. Many say, desiring to extinguish the Christian name, « There is no salvation. » Otherwise they would not hope to destroy the Church that was sprouting far and wide. « Upholder. » Because it was taken up in Christ and exalted with him. The head is he himself who first ascended into heaven.

VERS. 5.-- « And he hath heard me from the mount, etc. » That is, by Christ the prayer of the Church is heard, or its righteousness.

VERS. 6.-- « I have slept: » according to that word: [0848B] « Rise from the dead, and Christ shall enlighten thee [n: (Ephes. V)]. » It is no wonder that the Saviour says these things, when he did far greater things for the salvation of souls at that time when he was absent from the body, which things are recounted in the catholic epistle under the name of Saint Peter: « When he preached, having gone forth, to those spirits who were in prison, who had at one time been unbelieving [n: (I Petr. III)]. » [var: Vulg. 1 Pt 3:19 *spiritibus veniens praedicavit*, "coming, he preached to the spirits"; Migne prints *profectas*, an unconstruable feminine accusative for what the sense requires as *profectus*, "having gone forth."]

VERS. 7.-- « I will not fear thousands, » who try to extinguish the name of Christ.-- « Rise up. » O Christ our head, in whose resurrection is salvation.

VERS. 8.-- « For thou hast struck, etc. » Now that the Church reigns, the enemies have been struck with confusion. « The teeth of sinners, » that is, their cursing words; or the princes become teeth unto destruction. Therefore believe, O men, [0848C] that « salvation is the Lord's, » and, O Lord, « let thy blessing be upon thy people. With my voice. » These things are mine by desert, because « with my voice. » He who is good, and asks good things, cries with his own voice; with another's voice, that is, with one not according with his own life. « I have slept. » The end of the matter, whence he sets forth that there is nothing to fear. « I, » with weight; as though: they rage, but I would not sleep, unless I willed it. Or, I slept by consenting; I was made drowsy, by doing evil; I rose up, by forsaking sins. « For. » [n: (AUG.)] He does not weigh back, nor besides does he make safe because he has struck: but from thence the teeth were broken, because he struck; that is, the cursing words were brought to nothing; or, the teeth are those who cut off certain men from the number of the saints, and incorporate them among the evil.



## PSALM IV.

[0848D]

VERS. 1.-- « Unto the end. » [n: (AUG.)] The end is said in two ways, when something fails, or when it is completed. [n: (Ibid.)] A canticle indicates gladness. Psalms are those things which are sung to the psaltery, which the Prophet used in a great mystery. « A psalm, » concerning morals, for the doing of them, that the false gods and the vanities of the world may be forsaken; « Of a canticle, » because mention is made of the eternal delight.

VERS. 2.-- « When I called upon, etc. » [n: (CASS.)] By his own example he rebukes the unbelieving concerning false things. « Thou hast enlarged for me. » [n: (Ibid.)] From the straits of sadness thou hast led me into the breadth of joy. V. « We rejoice in tribulations, knowing that tribulation, etc. » [n: (Rom. V.)] [var: Vulg. Rm 5:3 *gloriamur in tribulationibus*, "we glory in tribulations."] He first showed that he had been heard: now, as though having God in his heart, [0849A] he speaks to him. « Have mercy on me. » He had mercy concerning righteousness and concerning the enlarging. Again, have mercy against the miseries of this life. « My prayer. » Concerning the good things that are to be asked for. And when it is thus concerning me, « Ye sons of men, how long will ye be heavy of heart? »

VERS. 3.-- « Ye love vanity, etc. » [n: (CASS.)] With your desire you embrace, with labour you seek vain idols, and lies, which are not God: or earthly things, which do not do what they promise.

VERS. 4.-- « And know ye, etc. » The new man being set forth, he bids them put off the old. [n: (AUG.)] Note that « And » is placed at beginnings, so that it may join the things said with the vision that is in the heart, so here, as: « Love not vain things. And know ye. » But the diapsalma forbids their being so joined. Diapsalma, according to Jerome, is always, the Hebrews, [0849B] Sela, that is, always, in confirmation of the preceding part. Sympsalma, that is, the joining of a psalm. « The Lord will hear. » Concerning rest it is thus, and so with you: and therefore cry out, being thus worthy to be heard.

VERS. 5.-- « Be ye angry. » If a motion of the soul arises which is not in our power, let not reason consent to it. [n: (CASS.)] A motion of the soul is not in our power, but by the grace of God we are able to temper it: what therefore belongs to custom, he permits; what belongs to fault, he forbids.

[n: (HIER.)] This the Apostle teaches: « Let not the sun go down upon your anger [n: (Ephes. IV)], » so that it is altogether a sin to be angry even lightly: but it is righteousness to soften anger by a swift repentance. « In your hearts. » [n: (AUG.)] Concerning those things which you handle in the heart, which God knows: that is, concerning consent; and concerning those things which you turn over [0849C] in the bed, that is, in the delight of the flesh, in which reason dwells captive, as a wild beast in its lair, « Be ye pricked, » through penance; or the beds are the thoughts of the fierce. [n: (CASS.)] Venial is the anger which is not carried through to effect. Diapsalma. « Sacrifice ye. » [n: (CASS.)] The old man being laid aside, we are bidden to be offered in sacrifice, because we are sure of good things. [n: (AUG.)] « The sacrifice of righteousness, » a contrite spirit, that, punishing itself, it may be slain to God: or, just works after penance, which the diapsalma marks, that from the old life there may be a passing over to the new, and so hope ye for good things. But because there is scarcely one who loves the inner goods, he adds:

VERS. 6.-- « Many say: Who showeth us good things? » Things to come, namely, of which they doubt and despair. Answering to which he shows briefly what [0849D] good things are to be sought.

VERS. 7.-- « The light is signed upon us, etc. » [n: (AUG.)] This light is the whole and the true good of man, wherewith he is signed, as a penny with the image of the king. « Light. » [n: (AUG.)] Light, that is, a shining countenance, and one that enlightens us, an image whereby thou art known. [n: (CASS.)] Or: the cross has been imprinted upon us, for a sign of our king, which is the light of the countenance: because in such men God shines out. The image of creation is reason; of re-creation, grace; of likeness, the whole Trinity. « In the heart. [n: (AUG.)] Not without in vain things, but within, where God dwells, is gladness to be sought.

VERS. 8.-- « From the fruit. » [n: (CAS.)] Because they think that in these things the good is consummated. These three, as being more suited to human [0850A] uses, he sets down for all riches.

VERS. 9.-- « In peace in the selfsame. » [n: (CASS.)] But I will sleep in the peace of the mind, here forgetful of the world, and I will rest in the time to come: because I am already in one hope, not in the manifoldness of the world. « In peace I will sleep and I will rest. » [n: (AUG.)] From all the things of the world, when this mortal shall put on immortality: and this will truly be, because it is already hope: and this is: « For thou, O Lord, » and assuredly that will be which is hoped for.



## PSALM V.

VERS. 1.-- « For her that obtaineth the inheritance. » Because he is honoured here to whom the inheritance is affirmed to belong, from which the rival is shut out. It is the Church, [0850B] which receives the inheritance, that is, eternal life, God himself, which here speaks of the inheritance which it asks for itself and asserts, saying that the rival is shut out. [n: (BEDA.)] That is, for the Church, which, at Christ's rising again, received the gifts of spiritual goods, which is itself also sometimes called the Lord's inheritance, purchased with his precious blood: whence it is said: « Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles, thy inheritance. » The whole psalm therefore is uttered in the person of the catholic Church, which in the first section asks that her prayer be heard, proclaiming that heretics and schismatics are to be shut out from the Lord's gifts. In the second section she prays that by the understanding of the divine Scriptures she may be directed by a straight path to that happy country, asserting that the faithless are thereby made utterly [0850C] strangers to it. At the last, calling to mind the rewards of the blessed, that by one preaching the punishment foretold might convert the wicked also, and the promised rewards rouse the just.

VERS. 2.-- « My words. » [n: (CASS.)] Here the prophet hints that a threefold prayer is to be made. For there are three principal vices in prosperity, three in adversity: against which we ought to make a threefold prayer. In prosperity, against the concupiscence of the flesh, against the concupiscence of the eyes, against the pride of life. In adversity, against the fear of death, of peril, of profit. [n: (Ibid.)] A threefold prayer: words, the psalmody of the mouth, a cry, the affection of the heart, therefore: « Thou shalt hear. » Behold, three times of the same thing. « With thine ears. » The ears of God are power, mercy. Power, whereby he can: mercy, [0850D] whereby he wills to hear; for unless there were mercy, he would hear no one's prayers.

VERS. 3.-- « To the voice. » That prayer has a voice which is worthy to be heard. « King. » [n: (AUG.)] Properly the Son, rightly first king, because through him one goes to the Father, whence he adds: And « my God: » and yet he does not say attend ye, but attend, because God is one.

VERS. 4.-- « For, etc. » [n: (AUG.)] Thus far the prayer, that it may be heard, etc., *as far as* and this in the morning, as soon as it forsakes the darkness.

VERS. 5.-- « In the morning I will stand. » [n: (CASS.)] Or, in the morning when eternity shall begin, and then I shall fully see that iniquity pleases not: because then it shall not dwell, « but the wicked shall be taken away, that he may not see the glory of God *(Isa. [0851A] XXVI)*: » [var: Vulg. Is 26:10 *et non videbit gloriam Domini*, "and he shall not see the glory of the Lord"; the Vulgate has nothing answering to *tolletur impius*] and then they shall not remain, even though they have had his mercy.

VERS. 6.-- « Neither shall the unjust remain. » Who do evil things. For thou hast hated those who work them, not those who have worked them.

VERS. 7.-- « Thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie. » [n: (AUG.)] Because this is contrary to truth. Truth is of that which is. A lie is not a substance or a nature, but is of that which is not, and deservedly is that destroyed which turns aside from that which is to that which is not. [n: (Ibid.)] To lie is to speak against that which is felt in the mind. [n: (Ibid.)] There are certain lies told for safety's sake, etc., *as far as* I did not consider that one raving could demand it back.

VERS. 8.-- « But I. » [n: (AUG.)] Thirdly, he says that he [0851B] will be the house of God, and that now he draws near in fear, before that consummation which casts out fear.

« I will go in. » [n: (CASS.)] By this I shall go in, because I shall adore. [n: (Ibid.)] He asks against those things which the rival brings in: whence she herself shall perish.

VERS. 9.-- « Lord, lead me. » [n: (AUG.)] Fourthly, making progress amid hindrances, he prays to be helped within, lest he be turned aside by deceitful tongues. « In thy justice. » [n: (CASS.)] Because thou receivest the penitent and the suppliant. « In thy sight. » [n: (AUG.)] Where man does not see, who is not to be believed whether he praise or blame: because he does not see into the conscience, in which the way to God is directed. Therefore he adds: « For there is no truth in their mouth. »

VERS. 10.-- « For there is not, etc. » Not only is there no truth in the mouth, but a sepulchre: because they bring forth stinking things [0851C] to corrupt, and if they do not prevail with them, they act deceitfully, that is, they do not only contrive, but accomplish.

VERS. 11, 12.-- « Judge them, O God. Let them fall from their thoughts. » He does not wish it, but foretells what shall be. He falls away who is disappointed of a good hope.

« And let them be glad. » [n: (CASS.)] After the retributions of the wicked he adds the rewards of the good, that as the punishment terrifies, so the rewards may incite.

VERS. 13.-- « As with a shield. [n: (CASS.)] In one word he indicates the free benefits of God. The will which calls is a defence against all things, and a crown, and a shield. Fitted to the head it is a crown, to the heart, a defence.



## PSALM VI.

[0851D]VERS. 1.-- « The octave » is the coming of the Lord, in which the sinner fears to be rebuked, and therefore repents. [n: (AUG.)] Some call the octave the coming of the Lord, etc., *as far as* whence the Church, fearing, here prays.

VERS. 2.-- « O Lord, not in thy fury. » [n: (BASIL.)] It is a deprecatory confession, which avails with God. First there is an exordium, in which he wins goodwill, by the power of the judge, by his own weakness, by the custom of sparing: because he wills to be entreated not by the dead, but by the living. « Rebuke. » [n: (AUG.)] To be rebuked is graver than to be accused, whence damnation is feared. To be chastised is milder, that is, to be amended or instructed. They are rebuked in the judgment, who are without a foundation.
